prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1271; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me at a light.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I had come to a stop behind a car at the light. I was completely stopped, maybe a few seconds, when I felt the hit from behind.

Q: How fast would you estimate the other vehicle was going?

A: I'm not sure. It didn't seem like a huge speed, but it was enough to push my car forward into the one in front of me.

Q: Did you see the other driver before the collision?

A: No, I didn't. I was looking at the light and the traffic ahead. I only saw their headlights in my mirror a moment before it happened.

Q: Were you injured, and if so, where?

A: My neck hurts, mostly on the back and left side. I've been stiff since it happened, and turning my head to check my blind spot is painful.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They said it looked like a neck strain and gave me a referral to follow up with my regular doctor.

Q: Did you have any pain before the collision involving your neck?

A: No, not that I can recall. I've had normal aches now and then, but nothing that stopped me from doing my job.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the incident?

A: Only that I've been cooperating with the police report and I'm hoping this can get resolved quickly, since I'm missing some work.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
